title: Defects found in the 1.3.0 merge review (verified in code)
description: Cheap, independent fixes that must land before the daemon becomes more central; each is one commit on its own fix/<slug> branch from origin/main, test shown failing first. Found by the 2026-10-08 external review of SUGGESTIONS-vcache-daemon.md and verified against the code.

title: rustc identity memo is keyed on path and size only; a same-size relink reuses the old banner
description: ResolveRustcFingerprint keys rustc-version-memo-v1 on realpath + size. ResolveCompilerId (C++) adds mtime and its comment explains why: relinking a compiler after a source change routinely lands on the same byte count. Add mtime, bump the memo name to v2. Fails first: a unit test that rewrites the fake rustc with same-size different bytes and a newer mtime and expects a new fingerprint.

title: util::ReadFile reads through istreambuf_iterator: 28% of vcache CPU on a warm build
description: perf on a warm 357-crate build: ReadFile 28%, BLAKE3 17%, memmove 9% of vcache's own CPU, which is 82% of all CPU in that build; the 550 MB asupersync entry takes 1.7 s to serve. Replace with fstat + a single read into a presized string (or mmap for blobs above a threshold) and remove the extra copies in DeserializeBlob/RestoreOutputs where a string_view suffices. Fails first: none applicable (no behaviour change); record the before/after warm wall time and perf share in the commit body instead.

title: Queued S3 upload is skipped when the disk layer evicts the entry first
description: UploadWorker re-reads the blob from disk; if DiskStorage::Put's inline LRU eviction removed it, the upload is counted as uploads_skipped and lost. Under cache pressure the newest entries are evicted first, so S3 silently loses exactly the latest work. Fix: the evictor skips keys with a pending/<key> journal marker (the journal is already the pin list). Fails first: an integration test with a tiny disk size and a mock S3 showing uploads_skipped stays 0.

title: Server::Enqueue dedupes by key, so a manifest re-Put is absorbed by an in-flight upload of the old value
description: queued_keys_ makes a second Put of the same key a no-op while the first upload is pending; manifests are mutable, so the newer states never reach S3. Fix: generation-aware enqueue (requeue when the value changed) or re-read the disk value at upload time and loop while it changed. Fails first: a unit test that two Puts of one key with different values end with the second value uploaded.

title: RestoreOutputs joins stored file names onto the output dir without a traversal check
description: A blob file name containing '..' escapes parsed.out_dir on a hit. Harmless with a single-user disk cache; material once blobs come from S3 or a peer. Reject names with '..' components or an absolute path at restore and at capture. Fails first: a unit test that a crafted blob is refused.

title: held_ hits are reported to the client as layer disk
description: HandleGet serves a blob from held_ (awaiting upload, disk layer absent) and labels the reply layer "disk", so the client counts kHitDisk while the daemon counts hits_memory. Fix: the daemon replies layer "memory"; the client logs that layer and still counts it as kHitDisk, because the stats file's nine positional lines are a format other tools read (adding a counter is a separate decision). Fails first: a unit test on the reply layer string for a held_ hit, and an integration test with disk disabled and the mock S3 that greps 'on memory' in VCACHE_LOG after a held_ hit.

title: Concurrent LoadManifest/StoreManifest cycles lose each other's states
description: Two compiles of one manifest key in different worktrees read the same states, each prepends its own and writes back; the second write drops the first's state. Merge on store (re-read, union by key, cap) instead of overwrite. Fails first: a unit test that two interleaved store cycles leave both states present.

title: Daemon as scheduler: single-flight keys, memory-aware admission, jobserver pool
description:
Make the 1.3.0 cache daemon the machine-wide coordinator for every compile and link that goes through vcache: compile a missed key once when several worktrees miss it together (single-flight), start a compile only when the machine can hold it (memory admission), and hand out job slots to ninja, make and cargo from one elastic pool (jobserver mode). Filed upstream as Unto-Labs/vcache#24; this epic is our implementation plan whether or not upstream takes it.

## Why

One 128-core / 125 GB host builds the same C++/Rust monorepo in several git worktrees at once (agents and humans). A `-O3 -ggdb3` C++ TU peaks near 3 GB, a release link above that. Every worktree runs its own `ninja -j N` / `cargo build`, each sized from the memory it saw at *its* start (sunbird's build.sh computes -j from MemAvailable once and says itself that ninja never retunes it), so two or three concurrent builds overcommit, swap, or lose a compiler to the OOM killer. After a shared-header edit every tree also recompiles the same ~400 TUs. vcache is the only process that already knows the key (dedup), could know the cost (admission) and spawns the compiler (realised memory), so the coordination belongs here rather than in a separate daemon that would need all three reported to it.

## What the daemon is today (verified 2026-10-08, dev 2c2c6e0)

A proxy for keys and blobs over a Unix socket: ops kHello, kGet, kPut, kStatus, kShutdown (daemon/protocol.h, kProtocolVersion = 1, unknown versions refused at hello). One connection per request (DaemonClient::RoundTrip closes after each), one thread per connection in Server::Serve, kMaxConnections = 1024, kReplyTimeoutSeconds = 300, Shutdown waits 60 s then shuts leftover fds. Counters are process totals (Server::counters_). held_ buffers blobs awaiting upload only when the disk layer did not take them. It never sees paths, roots, decisions, timings, pids or which tree a key belongs to; every feature here adds that through new ops. Measured on our 357-crate Rust workspace with a disk-only cache: warm 4.2-5.3 s off vs 4.8-5.4 s auto, cold ~115 s either way, raw cargo cold 108 s.

## Ground rules every child keeps

1. Daemon unavailable, refused, VCACHE_DAEMON=off, or the feature's own switch off: behaviour is exactly today's (compile in-process). No feature may turn a daemon failure into a build failure.
2. A lease or reservation is memory-only, dies with its client's socket, is never journalled, and is dropped on daemon restart (waiters are told to proceed locally). Speculative or read-only clients never hold one.
3. A waiting client still occupies a ninja/cargo job slot, so every wait is bounded and logged with its length.
4. kProtocolVersion becomes 2 in .8; an old daemon refuses at hello and the client falls back (rule 1).
5. One held connection per in-flight compile (a CompileSession, .8) carries lease, reservation and spawned-pid messages; RoundTrip's per-request connections stay for Get/Put. Shutdown closes sessions immediately instead of waiting on them; Idle() counts an open session as a client.
6. Every integration test asserts on VCACHE_LOG lines and --daemon-status rows, not only on exit codes, so a regression says which decision went wrong.

## Naming (bead ids cannot be renamed)

| concept | name | why |
|---|---|---|
| per-compile held connection | CompileSession (server), DaemonClient::OpenCompileSession, Op::kSessionOpen | joins Upload/UploadWorker naming; "session" alone fails out-of-context |
| single-flight hold on a key | KeyLease, Server::leases_ | the key is what is leased |
| ops | Op::kLeaseAcquire, kLeaseRelease, kMemoryReserve, kCompilerSpawned | join the Op enum; noun-verb states the purpose |
| memory grant | MemoryReservation, Server::reservations_ | |
| cost record | CompileCost {max_rss_kb, wall_ms, recorded_at}, CostKey, dir <cache>/costs/ | sibling of <cache>/compilers/ memos |
| ProcResult additions | max_rss_kb, wall_ms | units in the name |
| config | daemon.single_flight, daemon.admission, daemon.default_compile_kb, daemon.default_link_kb, daemon.jobserver, daemon.jobserver_jobs | join the [daemon] table; env VCACHE_DAEMON_<KEY> |
| CLI | --show-costs, --jobserver-env | join --show-stats / --daemon-status |
| counters (--daemon-status rows) | leases held / waiting / expired, compiles deduplicated; memory reserved_kb / realised_kb / reserve waits; jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn | |
| log markers (VCACHE_LOG) | "lease: ", "reserve: ", "jobserver: ", "cost: " | one topic word, like "rust manifest: " |
| fifo | <state dir>/jobserver.fifo | beside sock, lock, pending/ |

## Workflow for every child

Branch feat/<slug> from origin/main (our integration branch: upstream 1.3.0 + fork fixes; baseline make test 499 unit / 379 integration checks, 0 failed). export MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and keep /usr/lib64/ccache off PATH. Every new check is shown failing first and recorded as `Fails first:` in the commit body (AGENTS.md). Push the branch, merge --no-ff into main, push main:main. Commits that change the binary end with `Deploy: vcache`; rebuild dist/ with devtools' host-setup-buildcache.sh --force after the merge. Update docs/daemon.md and docs/configuration.md in the same commit as the feature. Do not touch the sibling repos' vcache-env.sh from these beads; .5 files those follow-ups.

## Order

.1 cost records and .8 compile sessions first (both small; admission reads .1, and .2/.3 sit on .8). .2 single-flight and .3 admission are then independent of each other. .4 fixed jobserver pool is independent too. .7 elastic pool needs .3 and .4. .5 build-tool integration needs .4 (and .7 for the elastic claim). .6 measurement last.

comments.author: richard
comments.text: Polished 3 rounds on 2026-10-08 (beads-workflow + scoped-naming): r1 inlined the design and ground rules so no bead cites the scratchpad doc, split the jobserver into fixed (.4) and elastic (.7) pools, added the naming table; r2 added .8 CompileSession/protocol v2 as the shared base of .2 and .3, made held replies and bounds explicit, added acceptance criteria; r3 verified no new name collides in src (CompileSession, KeyLease, MemoryReservation, CompileCost, CostKey, the log markers) and re-read every bead against the stored text. No cycles.

title: Cost records: wait4 peak RSS and wall time in blob meta, <cache>/costs/, and --show-costs
description:
## What

util::Run (src/util/subprocess.cc) waits with waitpid and throws resource usage away. Switch to wait4 and add to ProcResult: `uint64_t max_rss_kb` (ru_maxrss) and `uint64_t wall_ms` (monotonic clock around fork..wait). For the clang/gcc driver, wait4's ru_maxrss is the peak of the largest waited-for child, i.e. cc1plus/cc1, which is the number that matters; rustc is single-process; a link is the linker itself. Nothing else about Run changes.

Record the two numbers for every compile and link that vcache runs on a miss (RunCompile, RunRustCompile, RunLink; not dep-info or -E probes):
1. In the blob's meta string on store, as lines `max_rss_kb: N` and `wall_ms: N` after the existing `rustc:`/`crate:`/`roots:` lines (meta is informational and not part of any key, so no key bump).
2. In a CompileCost record under `<cache>/costs/<CostKey hex>`: a small text file with the last 8 observations (`max_rss_kb wall_ms recorded_at_unix`), written by the client with WriteFileAtomic (a lost race drops one observation, acceptable). CostKey = BLAKE3 of (operation: compile|rustc|link, canonical source path or link output path, language, codegen flag class). The flag class is the key_args with -I/-D/-include/paths removed, i.e. the optimisation and debug flags, so a miss on new content of the same file still has an estimate. Content is deliberately not in it.
3. `vcache --show-costs` prints per operation: records, p50 and max of max_rss_kb and wall_ms, and the 10 largest cost keys with their source path.

Estimate lookup (used by .3): max of the recorded max_rss_kb for the cost key; absent, the config default for the operation.

## Logging

VCACHE_LOG gets one line per recorded compile: `cost: <op> max_rss_kb=<n> wall_ms=<n> key=<costkey[0:16]> <source>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (tests/unit_test.cc, new Section "core::cost"): CostKey ignores content and roots but changes with the flag class and the operation; a CompileCost file round-trips and keeps only the last 8; the estimate is the max, not the mean.
- Unit: util::Run on a child that allocates 64 MB reports max_rss_kb >= 65536 and wall_ms within the measured bound.
- Integration (new section "9d. Cost records"): a compile's blob meta carries `max_rss_kb:` > 0; `--show-costs` lists the compile; `VCACHE_LOG` has the `cost:` line.

## Docs

docs/configuration.md: `--show-costs`; docs/design.md: what meta carries. Commit ends `Deploy: vcache`.
acceptance_criteria: make test green; unit Section core::cost and util::Run rusage checks fail on pre-fix code; integration 9d shows max_rss_kb in meta, --show-costs output and the cost: log line; Fails first lines in the commit body; docs updated; Deploy: vcache

title: Single-flight: KeyLease over a CompileSession so concurrent worktrees compile a missed key once
description:
## What Several worktrees that miss on one key compile it once. docs/design.md chose duplicate compiles deliberately for a single build, where a lock costs more than the duplicate; across worktrees the duplicate is real (a shared-header edit makes every tree recompile the same ~400 TUs). Switch: `daemon.single_flight = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_SINGLE_FLIGHT), default off until .6 has measured it. ## Protocol On the CompileSession from .8 (opened once the key is computed, closed after the outputs are restored or the compile has failed): - `kLeaseAcquire(key, bound_ms)` -> kOk + u8 outcome: `granted` (the session now holds the KeyLease), `stored` (the holder's kPut landed while we waited; do an ordinary kGet), or `compile` (holder failed or vanished, or bound reached). The daemon holds the reply for the waiter until one of those happens; the bound is the client's, computed from the holder's recorded wall_ms (from .1) that the first, immediate reply carries when the key is held: the client sends kLeaseAcquire once with bound_ms=0 to learn the holder's wall_ms, then once more with its bound. - `kLeaseRelease(key, outcome: stored|failed)` from the holder. HandlePut of that key also releases and wakes waiters. - A waiter's wait ends on: the holder's kPut (outcome stored), the holder's release with `failed` (compile), the holder's session closing without a release (compile), daemon shutdown (compile), or the bound (compile). - Bound: max(2 x holder wall_ms, 30 s), capped at kReplyTimeoutSeconds. A waiting wrapper still occupies a ninja/cargo job slot, so no unbounded wait. - Leases are memory-only, never journalled; a daemon restart drops them and reconnecting waiters are told to compile. A speculative or read-only (VCACHE_READONLY) client never acquires. - Concurrent S3 GETs of one key coalesce through the same table: the first Get of a missing-on-disk key fetches, later Gets of it wait for that fetch. ## Server KeyLease {key, holder session, acquired_at, holder_wall_ms, waiters}; Server::leases_ beside queued_keys_. A waiter's session thread blocks on the lease's condition variable with the bound as its timeout (one thread per connection, as today), never on a kGet. Session lifetime, shutdown and Idle() rules come from .8. Counters: leases held, leases waiting, leases expired, compiles deduplicated; --daemon-status rows for all four. ## Client RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink call acquire between key computation and the compile and release after store/failure. Waiters log every transition. ## Logging `lease: acquired `, `lease: waiting on holder pid

up to ms`, `lease: holder stored, serving hit after ms`, `lease: holder failed, compiling`, `lease: holder gone, compiling`, `lease: wait bound reached, compiling`, `lease: released `. ## Tests (fail first) - Unit (new Section "daemon::lease"): grant/deny per key; holder session close expires the lease and wakes waiters with "compile"; failed outcome wakes with "compile"; a stored outcome wakes with "get"; the wait bound arithmetic. - Integration (new section "10b. Single-flight"): two trees, same key, a fake compiler that sleeps 2 s and counts runs through a shared file, VCACHE_DAEMON=auto: exactly one `rust compile:`/`compile:` log line across both VCACHE_LOGs, one `lease: acquired` and one `lease: holder stored`, both trees' outputs byte-identical, `compiles deduplicated 1` in --daemon-status. A second run kills the holder (fake compiler exits 1): the waiter logs `lease: holder failed, compiling` and both trees finish. A third with the daemon stopped mid-wait: `lease: holder gone, compiling`. ## Docs docs/daemon.md: a "Single-flight" section with the rules above and the measured dedup count placeholder filled by .6. `Deploy: vcache`.
acceptance_criteria: daemon.single_flight off by default and byte-for-byte today's behaviour when off; unit Section daemon::lease; integration 10b: one compile across two trees, dedup counter 1, holder-failed and holder-gone paths each logged and both trees finish; Fails first recorded; docs/daemon.md Single-flight section; Deploy: vcache

title: Memory admission: kMemoryReserve against MemAvailable minus unrealised in-flight reservations
description:
## What

Start a compile or link only when the machine can hold it. Switch: `daemon.admission = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_ADMISSION), default off until .6 has measured it. Replaces each build's start-of-build `-j` guess with one machine-wide view across worktrees.

## Protocol (on the CompileSession from .8)

- `kMemoryReserve(cost_key, estimate_kb, bound_ms)` -> kOk + u8 outcome `granted` | `bound` (proceed unreserved after bound_ms, logged) + u64 waited_ms. The daemon holds the reply while the client waits; the session is dedicated, so holding it blocks nothing else. bound_ms defaults to 10 minutes.
- `kCompilerSpawned(pid)` right after util::Run forks, so the daemon can sample that pid.
- The reservation ends when the session closes (compile done or client gone).

## Admission arithmetic (server)

available_kb = MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (re-read at most once a second) minus unrealised_kb, where unrealised_kb = sum over in-flight reservations of max(0, estimate_kb - rss_kb(pid)), rss_kb sampled from /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS every 500 ms (0 until kCompilerSpawned). A resident compile is thereby not counted twice against MemAvailable. Grant when available_kb >= estimate_kb. FIFO queue of waiters, granted in order as reservations end or sampled RSS grows. Always at least one reservation in flight: an estimate larger than the machine is granted when nothing else holds one, so nothing deadlocks. Estimate = .1's cost table for the cost key, else daemon.default_compile_kb (default 2097152) / daemon.default_link_kb (default 4194304). v1 may skip RSS sampling and treat the whole estimate as unrealised for its first 10 s; the test seam below must then be respected by both forms.

Test seam: env VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO=<path> makes the daemon read that file instead of /proc/meminfo (undocumented outside tests, like the existing memo paths).

## Counters / status

reserved_kb, realised_kb, reserve waits, longest wait ms; --daemon-status rows "memory reserved / realised / waiting".

## Client

Reserve in RunCompile, RunRustCompile, RunLink after the key (and after a granted lease, if .2 is on: a lease waiter holds no memory) and before the compile; the dep-info and -E runs are not reserved (small). On any daemon error: proceed unreserved and log it (ground rule 1).

## Logging

`reserve: granted <kb> kB after <ms> ms (available <kb>, unrealised <kb>)`, `reserve: waiting (<available> < <estimate>) behind <n>`, `reserve: daemon unavailable, running unreserved`, server log `reserve: <pid> rss <kb> of <estimate>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (new Section "daemon::admission"): grant, refuse, FIFO order, the always-one rule, release on session close, realised RSS reducing the unrealised sum, and the cost-table-else-default estimate.
- Integration (new section "10c. Memory admission"): VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO points at a file with MemAvailable 3 GB, two compiles with 2 GB estimates (seeded cost files): the second logs `reserve: waiting` and is granted only after the first's `lease`/session ends; --daemon-status shows `reserve waits 1`; with the daemon stopped both run unreserved and log it.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md "Memory admission" with the arithmetic and defaults; docs/configuration.md for the keys. `Deploy: vcache`.
acceptance_criteria: daemon.admission off by default; unit Section daemon::admission incl. the always-one rule and FIFO order; integration 10c with VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO shows the second compile waiting then granted, and unreserved fallback with the daemon stopped; --daemon-status memory rows; Fails first recorded; docs; Deploy: vcache

title: Jobserver mode: a fixed fifo job-slot pool that ninja, make and cargo draw from
description:
## What

The daemon owns one GNU-make-style fifo job-slot pool for every build on the machine. Verified locally: ninja 1.13.2 follows `MAKEFLAGS=--jobserver-auth=fifo:PATH` when no -j is given on its command line (POSIX fifo form only; -l load limits still apply); GNU make 4.4.1 implements the fifo protocol; cargo 1.97 and rustc use the jobserver crate (.5 verifies the fifo form with strace before any sibling repo relies on it). This bead is the fixed-size pool; .7 makes it elastic.

## Behaviour

- `daemon.jobserver = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER) and `daemon.jobserver_jobs = N` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER_JOBS, default: online CPUs). On start the daemon creates `<state dir>/jobserver.fifo` (mkfifo 0600, same ownership rules as the socket) and writes N tokens ('+' bytes, as make does). It keeps a read-write fd open so the fifo never sees EOF.
- `vcache --jobserver-env` prints `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<path>` (and nothing else, exit 1 when no daemon or jobserver is running) for a build script to export. The `-j` with no count is what tells make it is a jobserver client.
- --stop-daemon removes the fifo; --daemon-status shows `jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn` (withdrawn is 0 until .7).
- A build started with the MAKEFLAGS but no daemon falls back to the tools' own defaults (ninja warns and uses its default -j; document that).

## Logging

`jobserver: pool <path> with <N> tokens`, `jobserver: removed <path>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (Section "daemon::jobserver"): fifo creation and removal, token count written, --jobserver-env output format.
- Integration (new section "10d. Jobserver"): with the daemon started with jobserver_jobs=2, a Makefile of 6 targets whose recipe is a fake compiler that sleeps 1 s and records its concurrent peers in a shared counter file; `make` under the exported MAKEFLAGS never records more than 2 peers; the same with a tiny build.ninja and `ninja` (no -j). Without the daemon the same make runs 6 wide.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md "Jobserver mode" with the version requirements and the exported line; docs/configuration.md keys. `Deploy: vcache`.
acceptance_criteria: daemon.jobserver off by default; fifo created/removed with the daemon; --jobserver-env prints the MAKEFLAGS line or exits 1; integration 10d: make and ninja (no -j) under the exported MAKEFLAGS never exceed jobserver_jobs concurrent fake compiles, and run wide without the daemon; Fails first recorded; docs; Deploy: vcache

title: Build-tool integration: verify cargo's fifo client, file the devtools and sunbird beads for MAKEFLAGS export
description:
## What

Cross-repo follow-up, closed when the sibling beads exist and the cargo check is recorded. The only change in this repo is the docs/daemon.md note from step 1.

1. Verify, with strace -f on one `cargo build` under `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<path>` from a daemon started with .4, that cargo and the rustc processes it spawns open the fifo and read tokens (cargo passes CARGO_MAKEFLAGS to rustc). Record the cargo/rustc versions and the strace lines in a comment on this bead and in docs/daemon.md. If cargo ignores the fifo, say so in the docs and stop here for Rust.
2. File a devtools bead: scripts/vcache-env.sh gains FBG_VCACHE_JOBSERVER=1, which starts the daemon with jobserver mode (and single_flight/admission as the owner decides) and exports its MAKEFLAGS from `vcache --jobserver-env`; the fifo lives under the per-OS store so host and el10 keep separate pools; document the contract (`FBG_VCACHE_JOBSERVER`, the exported MAKEFLAGS, that an existing MAKEFLAGS=-jN is replaced).
3. File a sunbird bead: build.sh and run_tests.sh stop passing -j to ninja when MAKEFLAGS carries --jobserver-auth (ninja ignores the fifo when -j is given), keep -l, and log "jobs: jobserver (<path>)" instead of the computed count; container.run.sh forwards MAKEFLAGS into el10.
4. Note in both that the daemon's socket and fifo paths must be reachable inside the container (upstream #23 part 2).

## Acceptance

The two sibling beads are created with the exact env contract above and linked here by id; the cargo verification is recorded.
acceptance_criteria: strace evidence that cargo and rustc read tokens from the fifo (or a documented negative) in docs/daemon.md and a comment here; devtools and sunbird beads created with the exact env contract and their ids noted here

title: Measure: tests/concurrent_worktrees_bench.sh over 2-3 worktrees per feature set, table in docs/daemon.md
description:
## What

A reusable benchmark script plus one measured table. `tests/concurrent_worktrees_bench.sh` (run by hand, like tests/linux_kernel_test.sh): takes a repo path, a build command, a worktree count (2 or 3) and a feature set; creates the worktrees under a scratch root, warms or clears the store as asked, starts the builds together, and records per build: wall time; minimum MemAvailable during the run (sample /proc/meminfo at 1 Hz into a CSV); OOM-killer events (dmesg -T since start, if readable); `compiles deduplicated`, `reserve waits`, `tokens withdrawn` from --daemon-status at the end; and the count of `lease: waiting` / `reserve: waiting` lines in each VCACHE_LOG. It prints one row per (feature set, worktree count) and leaves the CSVs beside the logs.

## Runs

On the 128-core / 125 GB host: the Rust workspace (357 crates; today 4-5 s warm, 115 s cold per worktree) and the C++ tree (~400 TUs) in 2 and 3 worktrees started together; feature sets: daemon off, single_flight only, +admission, +jobserver fixed, +jobserver elastic. Cold and warm each.

## Deliverables

The table in docs/daemon.md (replacing the placeholders .2-.7 left), the numbers posted on upstream #24 (no usernames, hostnames or repo names), and a recommendation per feature for the default in devtools' vcache-env.sh. If a feature measures no gain or a loss, say so and keep its default off.
acceptance_criteria: tests/concurrent_worktrees_bench.sh committed and documented; the table in docs/daemon.md for both trees, 2 and 3 worktrees, cold and warm, five feature sets; numbers posted on upstream #24 without identifying details; a default recommendation per feature recorded in the epic

title: Elastic jobserver pool: withdraw free tokens under memory pressure, restore when it clears
description:
## What

Make the jobserver pool from .4 elastic under memory pressure, using the admission view from .3. A token sitting in the fifo is a slot nobody is using, so the daemon can shrink the pool by reading free tokens back out and grow it by writing them back; a token held by a running job is never touched (the job returns it itself).

## Policy v1

Every 500 ms (the same tick that samples RSS): if there are reservations waiting in the admission queue, withdraw min(free tokens, waiting reservations) tokens; when the queue is empty and available_kb exceeds the largest default estimate, restore withdrawn tokens one per tick. Never withdraw below `daemon.jobserver_min_jobs` (default 2). The policy is one function over (free, withdrawn, waiting, available_kb) so it can be unit-tested and replaced.

## Counters / status

jobserver tokens withdrawn (now live), tokens restored total; --daemon-status shows them.

## Logging

`jobserver: withdrew <n> tokens (waiting <n>, available <kb> kB)`, `jobserver: restored <n> tokens`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit: the policy function on a table of (free, withdrawn, waiting, available) -> action rows, including the minimum floor and the one-per-tick restore.
- Integration (extends "10d"): jobserver_jobs=4, VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO at 3 GB, fake compiles with 2 GB estimates under make: the peer counter never exceeds 2 while reservations wait, and returns to 4 after they drain; both `jobserver: withdrew` and `jobserver: restored` appear in the daemon log.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md: the elastic policy and its floor. `Deploy: vcache`.
acceptance_criteria: policy function unit-tested on a table incl. the jobserver_min_jobs floor and one-per-tick restore; integration 10d extension shows the ceiling drop to 2 while reservations wait and return to 4 after; withdrew/restored log lines and status rows; Fails first recorded; docs; Deploy: vcache

title: CompileSession: one held connection per in-flight compile, protocol version 2
description:
## What

The shared scaffolding that single-flight (.2) and memory admission (.3) both build on, landed once so neither has to guess which comes first: a CompileSession, i.e. one held connection per in-flight compile, and protocol version 2.

## Protocol

- kProtocolVersion 1 -> 2. An old daemon refuses a v2 client at hello and the client falls back in-process; a v1 client is refused by a v2 daemon the same way (today's rule, unchanged).
- New op `Op::kSessionOpen` (after kHello on a fresh connection): marks the connection as a CompileSession. Reply kOk. Later ops on it (added by .2 and .3) may have their reply held by the daemon while the client waits; every held reply has a client-side bound and the daemon never holds a reply on a non-session connection.
- The session ends when the client closes the socket (outputs restored, compile failed, or the client died). Everything a session holds (added by .2 and .3) is released then.
- DaemonClient::OpenCompileSession(config) returns a session object whose destructor closes it; RoundTrip's one-connection-per-request behaviour is unchanged for Get/Put.

## Server

Sessions are tracked in Server::sessions_ (fd, client pid from SO_PEERCRED, opened_at). Shutdown closes sessions immediately with Status::kError "daemon shutting down" instead of waiting on them; Idle() counts an open session as a client; kMaxConnections = 1024 still bounds sessions plus requests, which covers -j-many compiles. Counter: sessions open; --daemon-status row "compile sessions N".

## Client

RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink open a session only when daemon.single_flight or daemon.admission is on (both off: no session, no new connection, so a daemon-off or unaware build is byte-for-byte today's). On any session error the compile proceeds as if there were no daemon and logs `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing`.

## Logging

`session: opened`, `session: closed after <ms> ms`, `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (Section "daemon::session"): a v1 hello is refused by a v2 daemon with the version named; a session survives a request on another connection; closing the fd ends the session; Shutdown with an open session returns without waiting the 60 s.
- Integration (new section "10a. Compile sessions"): with daemon.single_flight on and a running daemon, one compile logs `session: opened` and `session: closed`; with the daemon stopped mid-compile the compile still finishes and logs `session: daemon unavailable`; `compile sessions 0` in --daemon-status after the run.
